svg.text: One user message, end to end. Claude writes the answer; everything else is our code. Numbers are the real limits in the code.
Why ours: a search API returns ~500-char snippets. Pipedrive's snippet missed its
pricing table and the model quoted prices not in its source. So we buy only step 1.
Tavily (basic, 6 results) → Firecrawl v2 if it fails
breaker: 429 → 60 s · auth/credits → 1 h · else 2 min · 10-min cache
why: nobody can crawl the web; 2 providers = no single point of failure
top 5 pages in parallel · 4.5 s timeout · 3 MB cap
Mozilla Readability on linkedom · table cells kept as rows
why: we need the exact text we cite; price grids survive as rows
≤ 2 per search · official sites · text < 800 chars
or a price question with no price · /pricing ranked first
why: HubSpot's prices load only via JavaScript; renders cost credits
+1.5 for figures on numeric questions · best 2,400 chars/page
why: a page is too long for the model; the price table must beat the intro
[S#] · tier: official / primary / news / community / roundup
injection text removed · same page = same [S#] all chat
why: the model knows what to trust, and cites IDs, not URLs
Fallback: page can't be read → the provider's snippet, labelled "snippet only" + why
Memory — one local SQLite file (node:sqlite + FTS5, porter stemming) · memory/db.ts
Every table can be read and forgotten from the UI (/api/memory). Forgetting a chat removes everything derived from it.

Runs on the Claude Agent SDK (built without an API key). With an Anthropic API key, setting CLAUDE_RUNTIME=api swaps it for our own ~100-line loop (llm/messages-api.ts); same tool, memory and checks.
